body.en: Exponential functions model multiplicative physical phenomena where the instantaneous rate of change is proportional to the current state — governing radioactive decay, viral dissemination, financial growth, and cooling thermodynamics. Logarithmic functions serve as their continuous bijective inverses, mapping multiplicative scalings into linear coordinates. This chapter develops exponential and logarithmic foundations, derives differential growth and decay invariants, investigates the logistic saturation model, and introduces hyperbolic trigonometry.
body.ar: Exponential الدوال model multiplicative physical phenomena حيث the instantaneous rate of change is proportional to the current state — governing radioactive decay, viral dissemination, financial growth, and cooling thermodynamics. Logarithmic الدوال serve as their continuous bijective inverses, mapping multiplicative scalings into linear الإحداثيات. This chapter develops exponential and logarithmic foundations, derives differential growth and decay invariants, investigates the logistic saturation model, and introduces hyperbolic حساب المثلثات.

body.en: Master the structural properties of exponential functions with base b and natural base e, apply logarithmic laws to expand and condense expressions, and evaluate inverses.

body.en:
An exponential function with base \(b > 0\) (\(b \ne 1\)) is defined by \(f(x) = a b^x\). The function is strictly monotonic, has domain \(\mathbb{R}\), range \((0, \infty)\) (for \(a > 0\)), and horizontal asymptote \(y = 0\).

Euler's Number \(e\): The base of the natural exponential function is defined analytically by the continuous limit: \[ e = \lim_{n \to \infty} \left(1 + \frac{1}{n}\right)^n = \lim_{h \to 0} (1 + h)^{1/h} \approx 2.718281828459... \]

Algebraic Exponent Rules: \[ b^u \cdot b^v = b^{u+v}, \quad \frac{b^u}{b^v} = b^{u-v}, \quad (b^u)^v = b^{uv}, \quad b^{-u} = \frac{1}{b^u}, \quad b^0 = 1. \]
body.ar:
An exponential الدالة with base \(b > 0\) (\(b \ne 1\)) is defined by \(f(x) = a b^x\). The الدالة is strictly monotonic, has المجال \(\mathbb{R}\), المدى \((0, \infty)\) (for \(a > 0\)), and horizontal خط التقارب \(y = 0\).

Euler's Number \(e\): The base of the natural exponential الدالة is defined analytically by the continuous النهاية: \[ e = \lim_{n \to \infty} \left(1 + \frac{1}{n}\right)^n = \lim_{h \to 0} (1 + h)^{1/h} \approx 2.718281828459... \]

Algebraic Exponent Rules: \[ b^u \cdot b^v = b^{u+v}, \quad \frac{b^u}{b^v} = b^{u-v}, \quad (b^u)^v = b^{uv}, \quad b^{-u} = \frac{1}{b^u}, \quad b^0 = 1. \]

body.en:
Definition of Logarithm: For \(b > 0, b \ne 1\), and \(x > 0\): \[ y = \log_b x \iff b^y = x. \] The logarithmic curve has domain \((0, \infty)\), range \(\mathbb{R}\), and vertical asymptote \(x = 0\).

Fundamental Logarithmic Laws:

\[\log_b(uv) = \log_b u + \log_b v, \quad \log_b\left(\frac{u}{v}\right) = \log_b u - \log_b v, \quad \log_b(u^p) = p\log_b u.\]\[b^{\log_b x} = x, \quad \log_b(b^x) = x, \quad \log_b 1 = 0, \quad \log_b b = 1.\]

Change-of-Base Theorem: For any valid bases \(b\) and \(c\): \[ \log_b x = \frac{\log_c x}{\log_c b} = \frac{\ln x}{\ln b}. \] Proof: Let \(y = \log_b x\). Then \(b^y = x\). Taking the natural logarithm of both sides: \(\ln(b^y) = \ln x \implies y\ln b = \ln x \implies y = \frac{\ln x}{\ln b}\). \(\blacksquare\)
body.ar:

Fundamental Logarithmic Laws:

\[\log_b(uv) = \log_b u + \log_b v, \quad \log_b\left(\frac{u}{v}\right) = \log_b u - \log_b v, \quad \log_b(u^p) = p\log_b u.\]\[b^{\log_b x} = x, \quad \log_b(b^x) = x, \quad \log_b 1 = 0, \quad \log_b b = 1.\]

Change-of-Base مبرهنة: For any valid bases \(b\) and \(c\): \[ \log_b x = \frac{\log_c x}{\log_c b} = \frac{\ln x}{\ln b}. \] Proof: Let \(y = \log_b x\). Then \(b^y = x\). Taking the natural logarithm of both sides: \(\ln(b^y) = \ln x \implies y\ln b = \ln x \implies y = \frac{\ln x}{\ln b}\). \(\blacksquare\)

body.en:
Why Integration by Parts & Integrating Factors Work: Differentiating a product \(u(x)v(x)\) gives \((uv)' = u'v + uv'\). Integrating both sides and rearranging yields the Integration by Parts formula:

\[ \int u\,\frac{dv}{dx}\,dx = u v - \int v\,\frac{du}{dx}\,dx \]

Similarly, for a linear first-order ODE \(y' + P(x)y = Q(x)\), multiplying by the integrating factor \(\mu(x) = e^{\int P(x)\,dx}\) (which satisfies \(\mu'(x) = P(x)\mu(x)\)) collapses the left-hand side into an exact product derivative: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\bigl[\mu(x)y\bigr] = \mu(x)Q(x)\).
body.ar:
Why Integration by Parts & Integrating Factors Work: Differentiating a product \(u(x)v(x)\) gives \((uv)' = u'v + uv'\). Integrating both sides and rearranging yields the Integration by Parts الصيغة:

\[ \int u\,\frac{dv}{dx}\,dx = u v - \int v\,\frac{du}{dx}\,dx \]

Similarly, for a linear first-order ODE \(y' + P(x)y = Q(x)\), multiplying by the integrating factor \(\mu(x) = e^{\int P(x)\,dx}\) (which satisfies \(\mu'(x) = P(x)\mu(x)\)) collapses the left-hand side into an exact product المشتقة: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\bigl[\mu(x)y\bigr] = \mu(x)Q(x)\).

problem.en: Solve the logarithmic equation \(\log_2(x + 2) + \log_2(x - 4) = 4\) for all real solutions \(x\). Explicitly verify domain restrictions.
problem.ar: Solve the logarithmic المعادلة \(\log_2(x + 2) + \log_2(x - 4) = 4\) for all real الحلول \(x\). Explicitly verify المجال restrictions.

solution.en:
Step 1: State domain restrictions: Arguments must be strictly positive: \(x + 2 > 0 \implies x > -2\) and \(x - 4 > 0 \implies x > 4\). Intersection domain is \(x > 4\).

Step 2: Combine logarithms via product law: \[ \log_2[(x + 2)(x - 4)] = 4. \]

Step 3: Exponentiate in base 2: \[ (x + 2)(x - 4) = 2^4 = 16 \implies x^2 - 2x - 8 = 16 \implies x^2 - 2x - 24 = 0. \]

Step 4: Factor and test candidates: \[ (x - 6)(x + 4) = 0 \implies x = 6 \quad \text{or} \quad x = -4. \] Testing \(x = -4\): \(\log_2(-4+2) = \log_2(-2)\) is undefined in \(\mathbb{R}\), so \(x = -4\) is an extraneous root.

Testing \(x = 6\): \(\log_2(8) + \log_2(2) = 3 + 1 = 4\). Valid \(\checkmark\). Unique solution: \(x = 6\).
solution.ar:
Step 1: State المجال restrictions: Arguments must be strictly positive: \(x + 2 > 0 \implies x > -2\) and \(x - 4 > 0 \implies x > 4\). التقاطع المجال is \(x > 4\).

Step 2: Combine logarithms via product law: \[ \log_2[(x + 2)(x - 4)] = 4. \]

Step 3: Exponentiate in base 2: \[ (x + 2)(x - 4) = 2^4 = 16 \implies x^2 - 2x - 8 = 16 \implies x^2 - 2x - 24 = 0. \]

Step 4: Factor and test candidates: \[ (x - 6)(x + 4) = 0 \implies x = 6 \quad \text{or} \quad x = -4. \] Testing \(x = -4\): \(\log_2(-4+2) = \log_2(-2)\) is undefined in \(\mathbb{R}\), so \(x = -4\) is an extraneous root.

Testing \(x = 6\): \(\log_2(8) + \log_2(2) = 3 + 1 = 4\). Valid \(\checkmark\). Unique الحل: \(x = 6\).

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Analytical Application — Continuous Growth, Half-Life & Logistic Saturation

body.en: Model exponential decay and continuous compounding, calculate half-life and doubling time invariants, formulate Newton's law of cooling, and analyze logistic carrying capacity.
body.ar: Model exponential decay and continuous compounding, احسب half-life and doubling time invariants, formulate Newton's law of cooling, and analyze logistic carrying capacity.

label.en: ● Continuous Models, Doubling Time & Newton's Law of Cooling
label.ar: ● Continuous Models, Doubling Time & Newton's Law of Cooling (الدوال الأسية واللوغاريتمية والنماذج اللوجستية)

body.en:
Continuous Growth and Decay: \[ P(t) = P_0 e^{kt} \quad (k > 0: \text{growth}, \; k < 0: \text{decay}). \]

Doubling Time and Half-Life Invariants:

\[t_d = \frac{\ln 2}{k} \quad (k > 0), \qquad t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{|k|} = -\frac{\ln 2}{k} \quad (k < 0).\]

Newton's Law of Cooling: An object at initial temperature \(T_0\) in an ambient environment with constant temperature \(T_s\) cools according to: \[ T(t) = T_s + (T_0 - T_s)e^{-kt} \quad (k > 0). \]

Logistic Growth Model: When resources are finite, population growth is bounded by an environmental carrying capacity \(L\): \[ P(t) = \frac{L}{1 + C e^{-kt}} \quad (k > 0). \] As \(t \to \infty\), \(P(t) \to L\). The maximum growth rate occurs precisely at the inflection point where \(P = L/2\).
body.ar:

problem.en: The spread of a rumor in a high school of 1,200 students is modeled by the logistic function \(P(t) = \frac{1200}{1 + 39 e^{-0.6t}}\), where \(t\) is measured in hours after 8:00 AM. (a) How many students know the rumor initially at \(t = 0\)? (b) At what time \(t\) will half the school know the rumor? (c) Determine the carrying capacity \(L\).
problem.ar: The spread of a rumor in a high school of 1,200 students is modeled by the logistic الدالة \(P(t) = \frac{1200}{1 + 39 e^{-0.6t}}\), حيث \(t\) is measured in hours after 8:00 AM. (a) How many students know the rumor initially at \(t = 0\)? (b) At what time \(t\) will half the school know the rumor? (c) حدّد carrying capacity \(L\).

solution.en:
(a) Initial population at \(t = 0\): \[ P(0) = \frac{1200}{1 + 39 e^0} = \frac{1200}{1 + 39} = \frac{1200}{40} = 30 \text{ students}. \]

(b) Time to reach half population (\(P = 600\)): \[ 600 = \frac{1200}{1 + 39 e^{-0.6t}} \implies 1 + 39 e^{-0.6t} = \frac{1200}{600} = 2. \] \[ 39 e^{-0.6t} = 1 \implies e^{-0.6t} = \frac{1}{39}. \] Taking natural logarithms: \[ -0.6t = \ln\left(\frac{1}{39}\right) = -\ln(39) \implies t = \frac{\ln(39)}{0.6} \approx \frac{3.6636}{0.6} \approx 6.11 \text{ hours}. \] Half the school knows the rumor around 2:07 PM.

(c) Carrying capacity: As \(t \to \infty\), \(e^{-0.6t} \to 0\), so \[ \lim_{t \to \infty} P(t) = \frac{1200}{1 + 0} = 1200 \text{ students}. \]
solution.ar:
خطوات الحل:

(a) Initial population at \(t = 0\): \[ P(0) = \frac{1200}{1 + 39 e^0} = \frac{1200}{1 + 39} = \frac{1200}{40} = 30 \text{ students}. \]

(b) Time to reach half population (\(P = 600\)): \[ 600 = \frac{1200}{1 + 39 e^{-0.6t}} \implies 1 + 39 e^{-0.6t} = \frac{1200}{600} = 2. \] \[ 39 e^{-0.6t} = 1 \implies e^{-0.6t} = \frac{1}{39}. \] Taking natural logarithms: \[ -0.6t = \ln\left(\frac{1}{39}\right) = -\ln(39) \implies t = \frac{\ln(39)}{0.6} \approx \frac{3.6636}{0.6} \approx 6.11 \text{ hours}. \] Half the school knows the rumor around 2:07 PM.

(c) Carrying capacity: As \(t \to \infty\), \(e^{-0.6t} \to 0\), so \[ \lim_{t \to \infty} P(t) = \frac{1200}{1 + 0} = 1200 \text{ students}. \]

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced / University Rigor — Hyperbolic Trigonometry & Advanced Transcendental Systems

body.en: Formulate hyperbolic functions via exponential combinations, prove the hyperbolic Pythagorean identity, and solve advanced transcendental equations involving variable exponents.
body.ar: Formulate hyperbolic الدوال via exponential combinations, prove the hyperbolic Pythagorean المتطابقة, and solve advanced transcendental المعادلات involving المتغير exponents.

label.en: ● Hyperbolic Trigonometric Functions & Unit Hyperbola Identity
label.ar: ● Hyperbolic Trigonometric الدوال & Unit القطع الزائد المتطابقة

body.en:
Definition: Just as circular trigonometric functions parameterize the unit circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\), hyperbolic functions parameterize the right branch of the unit equilateral hyperbola \(x^2 - y^2 = 1\): \[ \cosh x = \frac{e^x + e^{-x}}{2}, \qquad \sinh x = \frac{e^x - e^{-x}}{2}, \qquad \tanh x = \frac{\sinh x}{\cosh x} = \frac{e^x - e^{-x}}{e^x + e^{-x}}. \]

Fundamental Hyperbolic Identity: \[ \cosh^2 x - \sinh^2 x = 1. \]

Proof: \[ \cosh^2 x - \sinh^2 x = \left(\frac{e^x + e^{-x}}{2}\right)^2 - \left(\frac{e^x - e^{-x}}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{e^{2x} + 2 + e^{-2x}}{4} - \frac{e^{2x} - 2 + e^{-2x}}{4} = \frac{4}{4} = 1. \quad \blacksquare \]
body.ar:
Definition: Just as circular trigonometric الدوال parameterize the unit الدائرة \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\), hyperbolic الدوال parameterize the right branch of the unit equilateral القطع الزائد \(x^2 - y^2 = 1\): \[ \cosh x = \frac{e^x + e^{-x}}{2}, \qquad \sinh x = \frac{e^x - e^{-x}}{2}, \qquad \tanh x = \frac{\sinh x}{\cosh x} = \frac{e^x - e^{-x}}{e^x + e^{-x}}. \]

Fundamental Hyperbolic المتطابقة: \[ \cosh^2 x - \sinh^2 x = 1. \]

Proof: \[ \cosh^2 x - \sinh^2 x = \left(\frac{e^x + e^{-x}}{2}\right)^2 - \left(\frac{e^x - e^{-x}}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{e^{2x} + 2 + e^{-2x}}{4} - \frac{e^{2x} - 2 + e^{-2x}}{4} = \frac{4}{4} = 1. \quad \blacksquare \]

problem.en: Find all exact real solutions to the transcendental equation \(x^{\ln x} = e^4 x^3\).
problem.ar: Find all exact real الحلول to the transcendental المعادلة \(x^{\ln x} = e^4 x^3\).

solution.en:
Step 1: State domain and apply natural logarithm: Since \(x\) is the base of a power and argument of \(\ln x\), the domain is strictly \(x > 0\). Taking \(\ln\) of both sides: \[ \ln\left(x^{\ln x}\right) = \ln\left(e^4 x^3\right). \] Applying the power and product rules: \[ (\ln x)(\ln x) = \ln(e^4) + \ln(x^3) \implies (\ln x)^2 = 4 + 3\ln x. \]

Step 2: Formulate quadratic in \(u = \ln x\): \[ u^2 - 3u - 4 = 0 \implies (u - 4)(u + 1) = 0. \]

Step 3: Solve for \(x\):

  • Branch 1: \(u = 4 \implies \ln x = 4 \implies x = e^4\).
  • Branch 2: \(u = -1 \implies \ln x = -1 \implies x = e^{-1} = \frac{1}{e}\).

Both values are strictly positive, satisfying \(x > 0\). The exact solution set is \[ x \in \left\{ \frac{1}{e}, e^4 \right\}. \quad \blacksquare \]
solution.ar:
Step 1: State المجال and apply natural logarithm: Since \(x\) is the base of a power and argument of \(\ln x\), the المجال is strictly \(x > 0\). Taking \(\ln\) of both sides: \[ \ln\left(x^{\ln x}\right) = \ln\left(e^4 x^3\right). \] Applying the power and product rules: \[ (\ln x)(\ln x) = \ln(e^4) + \ln(x^3) \implies (\ln x)^2 = 4 + 3\ln x. \]

Step 2: Formulate quadratic in \(u = \ln x\): \[ u^2 - 3u - 4 = 0 \implies (u - 4)(u + 1) = 0. \]

Step 3: أوجد قيمة \(x\):

  • Branch 1: \(u = 4 \implies \ln x = 4 \implies x = e^4\).
  • Branch 2: \(u = -1 \implies \ln x = -1 \implies x = e^{-1} = \frac{1}{e}\).

Both values are strictly positive, satisfying \(x > 0\). The exact الحل set is \[ x \in \left\{ \frac{1}{e}, e^4 \right\}. \quad \blacksquare \]

label.en: ⚠️ Common Traps & Exam Pitfalls — Exponentials & Logarithms
label.ar: ⚠️ أخطاء شائعة ومصائد الاختبار — Exponentials & Logarithms

body.en:
• Log Domain & Extraneous Roots: The argument of any logarithm must be strictly positive (\(x > 0\)). When solving equations such as \(\log(x) + \log(x-3) = 1\) by condensing to \(\log(x(x-3)) = 1\), the resulting quadratic may produce extraneous solutions that render the original individual arguments negative or zero. Always verify candidates in the uncombined equation!
  • Common False Log Rules: Remember that \(\log(A + B) eq \log A + \log B\), \( rac{\log A}{\log B} eq \log(A - B)\), and \((\log A)^p eq p\log A\). The power rule \(\log(A^p) = p\log A\) applies only when the exponent is attached directly to the inner argument.
  • Change of Base Order: \(\log_b a = rac{\ln a}{\ln b} = rac{\log_{10} a}{\log_{10} b}\). The argument \(a\) goes in the numerator, and the old base \(b\) goes in the denominator.
  • Continuous vs. Compounded Interest: Use \(A = Pe^{rt}\) strictly for continuous compounding. For compounding \(n\) times per year (e.g. monthly \(n=12\), quarterly \(n=4\)), use the discrete formula \(A = P\left(1 + rac{r}{n} ight)^{nt}\).
body.ar:
• Log المجال & Extraneous Roots: The argument of any logarithm must be strictly positive (\(x > 0\)). عندما solving المعادلات such as \(\log(x) + \log(x-3) = 1\) by condensing to \(\log(x(x-3)) = 1\), the resulting quadratic may produce extraneous الحلول that render the original individual arguments negative or zero. Always verify candidates in the uncombined المعادلة!
  • Common False Log Rules: Remember that \(\log(A + B) eq \log A + \log B\), \( rac{\log A}{\log B} eq \log(A - B)\), and \((\log A)^p eq p\log A\). The power rule \(\log(A^p) = p\log A\) applies only عندما the exponent is attached directly to the inner argument.
  • Change of Base Order: \(\log_b a = rac{\ln a}{\ln b} = rac{\log_{10} a}{\log_{10} b}\). The argument \(a\) goes in the numerator, and the old base \(b\) goes in the denominator.
  • Continuous vs. Compounded Interest: Use \(A = Pe^{rt}\) strictly for continuous compounding. For compounding \(n\) times per year (e.g. monthly \(n=12\), quarterly \(n=4\)), use the discrete الصيغة \(A = P\left(1 + rac{r}{n} ight)^{nt}\).

question.en: Solve the logarithmic equation \(\log_3(x + 6) + \log_3(x) = 3\) and eliminate any extraneous solutions.
question.ar: حل the logarithmic equation \(\log_3(x + 6) + \log_3(x) = 3\) and eliminate any extraneous solutions.

solution.en:
Combine the logarithms on the left-hand side using the product rule:

\[\log_3[x(x + 6)] = 3.\]

Convert to exponential form:

\[x(x + 6) = 3^3 = 27 \implies x^2 + 6x - 27 = 0.\]

Factor the quadratic:

\[(x + 9)(x - 3) = 0 \implies x = -9 \text{ or } x = 3.\]

Check the domain restrictions in the original equation:

  • For \(x = -9\): \(\log_3(-9)\) is undefined, so \(x = -9\) is an extraneous solution.
  • For \(x = 3\): \(\log_3(9) + \log_3(3) = 2 + 1 = 3\). Valid \(\checkmark\).

Therefore, the unique solution is \(x = 3\).
solution.ar:

\[\log_3[x(x + 6)] = 3.\]

\[x(x + 6) = 3^3 = 27 \implies x^2 + 6x - 27 = 0.\]

حلّل the quadratic:

\[(x + 9)(x - 3) = 0 \implies x = -9 \text{ or } x = 3.\]

Check the domain restrictions in the original equation:

  • For \(x = 3\): \(\log_3(9) + \log_3(3) = 2 + 1 = 3\). Valid \(\checkmark\).

وبالتالي، the unique solution is \(x = 3\).

question.en: A radioactive substance follows the decay model \(M(t) = M_0 e^{-kt}\). If 20% of the sample decays in 15 days, find the exact decay constant \(k\) and the substance's half-life in days to the nearest tenth.
question.ar: A radioactive substance follows the decay model \(M(t) = M_0 e^{-kt}\). إذا كان 20% of the sample decays in 15 days, أوجد exact decay constant \(k\) and the substance's half-lإذا كانe in days مقرباً إلى أقرب tenth.

solution.en:
If 20% decays in 15 days, then 80% remains at \(t = 15\):

\[0.80 M_0 = M_0 e^{-15k} \implies e^{-15k} = 0.80.\]

Take the natural logarithm of both sides:

\[-15k = \ln(0.80) \implies k = -\frac{\ln(0.80)}{15} = \frac{\ln(1.25)}{15} \approx 0.01488\text{ day}^{-1}.\]

The half-life \(t_{1/2}\) satisfies \(e^{-k t_{1/2}} = 0.5\):

\[t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{k} = \frac{15\ln 2}{-\ln(0.80)} \approx \frac{15(0.6931)}{0.2231} \approx 46.6\text{ days}.\]

question.en: [Practice 3 · Easy] Consider the exponential function \( f(x) = 2^x \). What is the value of \( f(3) \)?
question.ar: [Practice 3 · Easy] Consider the exponential function \( f(x) = 2^x \). ما قيمة \( f(3) \)?

hints.en: The function is given by \( f(x) = 2^x \).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( f(x) = 2^x \) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: To find \( f(3) \), we substitute \( x = 3 \) into the function: \( f(3) = 2^3 \). Calculating the power, \(2^3 = 2 \times 2 \times 2\).
hints.ar: To أوجد \( f(3) \), we عوّض \( x = 3 \) into the function: \( f(3) = 2^3 \). Calculating the power, \(2^3 = 2 \times 2 \times 2\).

solution.en: The function is given by \( f(x) = 2^x \). To find \( f(3) \), we substitute \( x = 3 \) into the function: \( f(3) = 2^3 \). Calculating the power, \( 2^3 = 2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8 \). Therefore, the value of \( f(3) \) is 8.
solution.ar: The function is given by \( f(x) = 2^x \). To أوجد \( f(3) \), we عوّض \( x = 3 \) into the function: \( f(3) = 2^3 \). Calculating the power, \( 2^3 = 2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8 \). وبالتالي، the value of \( f(3) \) is 8.

question.en: [Practice 4 · Medium] The graph of the function \( f(x) = a \cdot b^x \) passes through the points \((1, 12)\) and \((3, 108)\). Determine the value of the parameter \(a\).
question.ar: [Practice 4 · Medium] The graph of the function \( f(x) = a \cdot b^x \) يمر بالنقطة the points \((1, 12)\) and \((3, 108)\). حدّد value of the parameter \(a\).

hints.en: We are given the function \( f(x) = a \cdot b^x \) and two points it passes through: \((1, 12)\) and \((3, 108)\).
hints.ar: We are given the function \( f(x) = a \cdot b^x \) and two points it يمر بالنقطة: \((1, 12)\) and \((3, 108)\).

hints.en: Using the first point \((1, 12)\), we have: \( 12 = a \cdot b^1 \) (Equation 1) Using the second point \((3, 108)\), we have: \( 108 = a \cdot b^3 \) (Equation 2).
hints.ar: باستخدام first point \((1, 12)\), we have: \( 12 = a \cdot b^1 \) (Equation 1) باستخدام second point \((3, 108)\), we have: \( 108 = a \cdot b^3 \) (Equation 2).

hints.en: Therefore, the value of the parameter \(a\) is 4.
hints.ar: وبالتالي، the value of the parameter \(a\) is 4.

solution.en:
We are given the function \( f(x) = a \cdot b^x \) and two points it passes through: \((1, 12)\) and \((3, 108)\).

Using the first point \((1, 12)\), we have:
\( 12 = a \cdot b^1 \)  (Equation 1)

Using the second point \((3, 108)\), we have:
\( 108 = a \cdot b^3 \) (Equation 2)

To find \(a\) and \(b\), we can divide Equation 2 by Equation 1:
\( \frac{108}{12} = \frac{a \cdot b^3}{a \cdot b^1} \)
\( 9 = b^2 \)
Taking the square root of both sides, and assuming \(b > 0\) for exponential functions:
\( b = 3 \)

Now, substitute the value of \(b=3\) back into Equation 1:
\( 12 = a \cdot 3^1 \)
\( 12 = 3a \)
Divide by 3 to solve for \(a\):
\( a = \frac{12}{3} \)
\( a = 4 \)

Therefore, the value of the parameter \(a\) is 4.
solution.ar:
We are given the function \( f(x) = a \cdot b^x \) and two points it يمر بالنقطة: \((1, 12)\) and \((3, 108)\).

باستخدام first point \((1, 12)\), we have:
\( 12 = a \cdot b^1 \)  (Equation 1)

باستخدام second point \((3, 108)\), we have:

To أوجد \(a\) and \(b\), we can divide Equation 2 by Equation 1:
\( \frac{108}{12} = \frac{a \cdot b^3}{a \cdot b^1} \)
\( 9 = b^2 \)
Taking the square root of both sides, and assuming \(b > 0\) for exponential functions:

\( a = 4 \)

وبالتالي، the value of the parameter \(a\) is 4.

label.en: ● Master Atlas of the 9 Main Parent Functions & Universal Transformation Law
label.ar: ● الأطلس الشامل للدوال الأم التسع وقانون التحويلات الهندسية العام

body.en:
Every algebraic and elementary transcendental model is built by transforming one of the nine core parent functions via \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\), where \(|a|\) scales vertically (reflecting across the \(x\)-axis if \(a < 0\)), \(h\) shifts horizontally, and \(k\) shifts vertically:

FamilyTransformed Form \(g(x)\)DomainRange (\(a > 0\))Key Geometric Feature
Constant\(f(x) = c\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\{c\}\)Horizontal line, slope \(0\)
Linear\(a(x - h) + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Constant slope \(m = a\), pivot \((h, k)\)
Quadratic\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Parabola vertex \((h, k)\), axis \(x = h\)
Cubic\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Inflection center \((h, k)\), S-curve
Absolute Value\(a|x - h| + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)V-corner vertex \((h, k)\), slopes \(\pm a\)
Radical\(a\sqrt{x - h} + k\)\([h, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Endpoint \((h, k)\), half-parabola
Rational\(\dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\)\(x \neq h\)\(y \neq k\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), horizontal \(y = k\)
Exponential\(a \cdot 2^{x - h} + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((k, \infty)\)Horizontal asymptote \(y = k\), anchor \((h, a+k)\)
Logarithmic\(a\ln(x - h) + k\)\((h, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), anchor \((h+1, k)\)
body.ar:
تُبنى النماذج الجبرية والمتسامية الأساسية من خلال تطبيق التحويل القياسي \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\) على إحدى الدوال الأم التسع، حيث يتحكم \(|a|\) في التمدد الرأسي (مع انعكاس حول محور السينات إذا كان \(a < 0\))، ويمثل \(h\) الإزاحة الأفقية، و\(k\) الإزاحة الرأسية:

عائلة الدالةالصورة المحوّلة \(g(x)\)المجالالمدى (\(a > 0\))السمة الهندسية المميزة
الثابتة\(f(x) = c\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\{c\}\)مستقيم أفقي ميله \(0\)
الخطية\(a(x - h) + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)ميل ثابت \(m = a\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h, k)\)
التربيعية\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)قطع مكافئ رأسه \((h, k)\) ومحوره \(x = h\)
التكعيبية\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)نقطة انعطاف مركزية \((h, k)\)
القيمة المطلقة\(a|x - h| + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)رأس زاوي على شكل V عند \((h, k)\) بميلين \(\pm a\)
الجذرية\(a\sqrt{x - h} + k\)\([h, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)نقطة بداية \((h, k)\) ومجال مقيّد \(x \ge h\)
النسبية (المقلوب)\(\dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\)\(x \neq h\)\(y \neq k\)تقارب رأسي \(x = h\) وتقارب أفقي \(y = k\)
الأسية\(a \cdot 2^{x - h} + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((k, \infty)\)تقارب أفقي \(y = k\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h, a+k)\)
اللوغاريتمية\(a\ln(x - h) + k\)\((h, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)تقارب رأسي \(x = h\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h+1, k)\)
